auditableEventSource.mouse: WH_MOUSE_LL emits WM_MOUSEMOVE, WM_LBUTTONDOWN, and WM_LBUTTONUP with coordinates from MSLLHOOKSTRUCT.pt

coordinateContract.nativeMouse: MSLLHOOKSTRUCT.pt is physical Windows screen pixels
coordinateContract.window: Electron BrowserWindow.getBounds() is retained as DIP and converted by screen.dipToScreenRect(source, dip)
coordinateContract.hitTest: only the converted physical rectangle is compared with native mouse coordinates
coordinateContract.trace: records DIP bounds, physical bounds, display scaleFactor, and units

inputTrustContract: candidate arming and commit require WH_MOUSE_LL events with injected:false; injected:true or missing flags are logged and ignored

attempts.method: Win32 SendInput driver with the original WH_MOUSE_LL helper
attempts.result: The helper was ready but observed no mouse events; no claim is made that the hook itself is unavailable to physical input.
The controller rejected endpoint (-90, 190) because it was outside the target window, so it cannot produce the required external release.

conclusion: A physical-mouse trace remains required. The prior polling helper is deliberately removed because button-state reads and cursor reads are not an atomic release event.
